title: n-roth12-DFSLineupOptimizer
universal_lens: NFL DFS lineup optimization as a constrained combinatorial set-covering problem with discrete projection inputs and fixed-format outputs. The CSV-in/CSV-out contract enables offline optimization via FPPG projections, bridging slate authenticity and projection reliability through structured data interfaces.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference on lineup likelihood under observed salary and FPPG constraints using conformal predictive distributions over player eligibility sets. GSI employs Bayesian inference over parsed CSV slates to compute posterior belief distributions on player performance, conditioning on historical FPPG and contest-specific constraints.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning engine models lineup state transitions via deterministic constraint satisfaction with user-defined team stack inputs. GSE implements a state-transition system where slate authenticity is toggled between synthetic (sample) and real (CSV-pulled) modes, using FPPG as kernel for lineup optimization.

primitives.name: Discrete Fantasy Sports Lineup Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: Vision A small, dependency-free Python optimizer for NFL DFS: reads a contest CSV (DK/FD/Yahoo salaries), optimizes one lineup or generates many, supports full-roster, Captain, and MVP formats, exports entry-ready CSVs.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L': 'set of lineups, dimensionless', 'P': 'set of players, dimensionless', 'S': 'salary cap, USD', 'F': 'fantasy points per game, FPPG'}
primitives.assumptions: Players are assigned fixed FPPG values; lineup constraints are deterministic and static.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When |L| > 1, combinatorial explosion occurs without pruning heuristics.

layer2.mapping: Each lineup L ∈ L maps to a binary selection vector over P with cardinality bounded by roster size; FPPG sum is maximized subject to S constraint.
layer2.telemetry: Number of valid lineups generated per second.

primitives.name: Naive Projection Input Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: • No simulation, no ownership, no stacking beyond userspecified team stacks; projection input is naive (FPPG from the salary file) — the repo is honest that this is a placeholder for real projections.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p_i': "player i's projected FPPG, FPPG", 'C': 'contest CSV, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Projected FPPG is independent of opponent strength or matchup dynamics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When p_i varies significantly across players, model becomes unreliable.

layer2.mapping: Input FPPG values p_i define a static utility function U(p_i) used in objective maximization.
layer2.telemetry: Mean absolute error between p_i and actual performance.

primitives.name: Constraint Satisfaction System
primitives.verbatim_quote: from the DK/FD/Yahoo contest page. Built-in-modules only; pip install lineup-optimizer from PyPI. 3. Constraints • License:
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C_s': 'salary constraint, USD', 'C_r': 'roster constraint, count', 'T': 'team stack specification, boolean matrix'}
primitives.assumptions: All constraints are hard-coded and non-negotiable.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When T is inconsistent with C_s or C_r, no valid solution exists.

layer2.mapping: Each valid lineup satisfies a system of linear inequalities defined by C_s, C_r, and T.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage of feasible solutions among total candidate combinations.

primitives.name: Offline Processing Unit
primitives.verbatim_quote: Explicitly offline — projections come from the salaries CSV's fantasy-points-per-game column unless the user edits them.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'O': 'offline processing flag, boolean', 'I': 'input data stream, CSV', 'R': 'output result set, CSV'}
primitives.assumptions: All computations occur without external API calls or live data feeds.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When I is malformed or missing, O fails to produce R.

layer2.mapping: O defines a deterministic data pipeline from I to R, bypassing real-time updates.
layer2.telemetry: Time elapsed from I ingestion to R generation.

primitives.name: Offline FPPG Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: GSE lens The instructive part is what it admits: it runs offline and uses FPPG as a stand-in projection, and it says so up front.
primitives.assumptions: FPPG serves as proxy for player expected value under static game conditions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When live slate data unavailable, FPPG becomes sole predictive input.

layer2.mapping: FPPG is derived from historical performance data and used as core input in GSE's optimization engine when real-time data is absent.
layer2.telemetry: Mean absolute error between projected and actual FPPG in test slates

primitives.name: CSV Slate Contract
primitives.verbatim_quote: The repo's real lesson is the CSV-in/CSV-out contract with the contest page: a live slate feed doesn't have to be an API — DK/FD publish player pools as downloadable CSVs per contest.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_{csv}': 'CSV-sourced slate (set of players)', 'C': 'Contest identifier (unitless)', 'T': 'Time of download (seconds since epoch)'}
primitives.assumptions: DK/FD player pools are deterministic and consistent within contest scope.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When API access is unavailable, CSV-based slate generation substitutes.

layer2.mapping: The CSV slate is isomorphic to the real-time slate under fixed contest parameters.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of parsed CSV vs. official slate in terms of player eligibility and lineup validity

primitives.name: Synthetic vs Real Slate Duality
primitives.verbatim_quote: GSE's optimizer falls back to a sample slate — functionally the same honesty, but inverted: the projections are (becoming) real while the slate is fake.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_{real}': 'Real-time slate (set of players)', 'S_{synth}': 'Synthetic slate (set of players)', 'P_{real}': 'Real projections (vector of FPPG)', 'P_{synth}': 'Synthetic projections (vector of FPPG)'}
primitives.assumptions: Projections are more reliable than slate accuracy in absence of live data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Inverted duality where slate is synthetic but projections are real.

layer2.mapping: The optimizer treats synthetic slate as placeholder while relying on real-time projection logic.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation between synthetic slate and real slate in lineup outcomes

primitives.name: Scheduled CSV Puller
primitives.verbatim_quote: GSE's "no live slate feed" gap could be closed with a scheduled CSV puller as the v1 producer, no API partnership required.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P_{pull}(t)': 'Pull schedule function (seconds)', 'C(t)': 'Contest state at time t (unitless)', 'D_{csv}(t)': 'Downloaded CSV data at time t (bytes)'}
primitives.assumptions: Scheduled pulls can maintain slate relevance without real-time API.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When no live feed exists, scheduled pull ensures periodic slate updates.

layer2.mapping: Scheduled pull mimics live feed behavior by updating slate periodically.
layer2.telemetry: Latency between CSV download and slate availability in optimizer

It highlights that despite the absence of a live slate feed, the system remains viable through structured data ingestion and projection logic. The key insight is that CSVs serve as a stable interface for player pools, enabling a robust optimization workflow even without real-time APIs. This approach aligns with principles of conformal prediction and Bayesian inference, where uncertainty is quantified and managed through historical data. The document also underscores the importance of maintaining a clear separation between slate authenticity and projection reliability, suggesting that synthetic slates can be acceptable if projections remain accurate. This duality is central to GSE’s design philosophy, allowing for resilience in data availability while preserving analytical rigor. The practical implication is that a minimal viable product (MVP) can be built using scheduled CSV pulls, which bypasses the need for complex API integrations and provides a working solution immediately. This pragmatic stance reflects a broader trend in algorithmic sports analytics toward modular, data-driven systems that prioritize correctness and adaptability over real-time responsiveness.
